newsitem.title: USA: IXC to sell $200 mln PIK prfd stock-sources.
newsitem.headline: IXC to sell $200 mln PIK prfd stock-sources.

text.p: IXC Communications Inc has decided to offer $200 million in junior subordinated exchangeable payable-in-kind (PIK) preferred stock after consulting with bondholders, according to sources close to the situation.

The company had met resistance from bondholders on its original plan to issue $250 million in additional senior notes that would have the same right of payment as its outstanding 12.5 percent senior notes due '05, sources said.

The "bondholder-friendly" issue of junior preferred stock will be exchangeable for subordinated debt and will allow the company to raise additional funds without violating covenants on its outstanding senior notes.
Proceeds from the deal will be used to expand the company's long-distance fiber-optic network, a source said.
IXC and lead underwriter, Credit Suisse First Boston, will begin the roadshow for the offering on Wednesday.

For the first three years, IXC will have the option to make either PIK or cash payments on the exchangeable preferred stock. Subsequently, the securities, which will have 12-year maturities and will be non-callable in five years, will pay only in cash. The preferred stock will also be junior to an outstanding issue of cumulative preferred stock, sources said
Seperately, IXC will extend the deadline for a consent solication for bondholder approval of a variety of other financial transactions, sources said.
IXC, based in Austin, Texas, owns and operates a nationwide long-distance digital telecommunications network.
